metadata.title: Scientific Claim Registry (SCR): A Versioned Memory of How Scientific Answers Evolve — Framework v0.5: Unattended Layer 1 Surveillance at Library Scale, with Documented Failure Modes
metadata.description:
Positioning: PubMed stores scientific papers. ScientificClaims.org stores the evolving answers to scientific questions. The Scientific Claim Registry (SCR) is infrastructure for the memory of science — not its truth, consensus, or recommendations. It registers, it does not arbitrate.

What v0.5 adds over v0.4: v0.4 made every evidence link independently verified. v0.5 is the first version in which the registry has been kept current by its own Layer 1 surveillance loop (retrieve → classify → dual-model verify → promote/corroborate → recompile → version), and it reports what that took, including where it failed.

Growth through the loop, not manual curation. From v0.4 to v0.5 the lipedema pilot grew from 347 to 526 evidence claims and from 423 to 626 evidence records (895 question–claim links, 383 distinct DOIs) under the same 42 versioned questions. Sources: (1) an unattended weekly rotating contradiction sweep (R-AI-12), June–September 2026, pairing each topical retrieval with a null/negative/opposing-evidence pass; (2) a library-scale backfill re-running all 42 questions against the author’s curated lipedema library (4,563 structured records) plus Europe PMC. Verification across the registry: 614 verified, 5 disputed (kept and flagged), 7 unverified; 19 records contradict the claim they sit under. Each changed answer received a new immutable version with a “what changed” note.

Operational honesty. Unattended operation exposed failures a demo never shows, documented with the guarantees added: (a) eight silent weeks in which a missing LLM credential made every run fail while the rotation still advanced and logged the questions as swept — the rotation now advances only on successful runs, and a missing credential is a loud warning; (b) silently degraded semantic retrieval, now with keyword fallback and a self-started library service; (c) a malformed model response that discarded a whole run (atomic writes kept the registry intact), now parsed leniently on retry. A memory system that hides its own gaps contradicts its premise.

Object model (unchanged). The scientific question (e.g. SQ-LIP-000007) is the primary navigable object. Underneath it, claims (SCR-LIP-000001) are structured, versioned units of evidence with an explicit role (supporting / contradicting / refines / context), PECO context, a GRADE rating, dated provenance, a change log, sentence-level provenance and an independent verification verdict.

Prior-art honesty: SCR does not invent the claim primitive or persistent claim identity — nanopublications/Trusty URIs, micropublications, Wikidata, CIViC, ClinGen, Epistemonikos/PICO, SciFact, GRADE and MAGICapp already exist. The v0.5 contribution is evidence that a question-centric, verified, versioned registry can be maintained by its own loop, with the failure modes of unattended operation documented and guarded. Operated by the BIO (Biological Intelligence Observatory) research method.
